title: CMOS Fabrication Steps
intro: Knowing how a chip is made explains many analog constraints: matching, parasitics, minimum sizes and latch-up.

items: Wafer processing: purified silicon is grown as a crystal ingot, sliced into wafers and polished.
Photolithography: a light-sensitive resist is patterned through a mask; the minimum feature is about k1 * wavelength / NA.
Oxidation: heating silicon in oxygen grows silicon dioxide for gate insulator and isolation.
Ion implantation: dopant ions are accelerated into silicon to form wells, sources, drains and threshold adjusts, followed by annealing.
Deposition and etching: polysilicon gates, dielectrics and metal layers are deposited and patterned by etch.
Device fabrication: a typical flow forms wells, isolation (STI), gate oxide and poly, source/drain implants, silicide, then multiple metal layers with vias.

blocks.text: An n-well CMOS process contains parasitic PNP and NPN bipolar transistors that form a thyristor (SCR). A transient can trigger it, shorting supply to ground. Prevent it with substrate and well contacts near every transistor, guard rings and adequate spacing between NMOS and PMOS.

blocks.title: Lithography limit
blocks.text: 193 nm light, numerical aperture 1.35 (immersion), k1 = 0.3: what is the smallest printable half-pitch?

blocks.title: Latch-up prevention
blocks.text: Name two layout rules that reduce the risk of latch-up.
solution: Place well and substrate taps close to each transistor (low well/substrate resistance reduces the trigger voltage) and surround NMOS or PMOS devices with guard rings; increase spacing between N+ and P+ regions of the two device types.
